clue.text: The German diamonds holding I have acquired

indicators.note: the first pieces hold the next one within them, gripping it like a hand

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for 'the'
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
I've is the contraction of 'I have'

explanation.surface: Some German gems have come into my possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diamonds' looks like part of the gem picture but is just the card-suit letter; 'holding' sets the contraction inside the German article plus that letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obtained from a source or gained is said to be derived or acquired.

clue.text: Monster to slowly move leg

parts.note: to drag is to move slowly and heavily
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A beast drags its leg along slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fire-breathing winged beast of legend is a classic monster.

clue.text: One fleeing another country, last to leave resort

indicators.note: the final letter departs from the word for an exile

parts.note: a refugee flees their homeland

explanation.surface: An asylum seeker departs a holiday destination last.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a place of shelter one turns to, as in 'last resort'.

clue.text: Workers who won't get ready?

parts.note: 'ready' is slang for cash, so these are workers who go unpaid

explanation.surface: Some staff refuse to prepare themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpaid helpers offer their labour freely without receiving money.

clue.text: Doctor starts to use more surgical instruments

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A doctor begins using more surgical tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: percussion instruments struck with sticks are a kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: Small and crazy, grabbing the woman under the table

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: the word for crazy seizes the next piece and holds it inside

parts.note: crazy means mad
a woman is referred to as she

explanation.surface: A short, wild woman has ended up drunk on the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under the table' is the idiom for being too drunk to stand, so it defines a slang word for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: someone drunk enough to slide under the table is heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Bad scent — is it Kelvin, perhaps?

indicators.note: a bad version of these letters is a jumbled one

explanation.surface: Asking whether a nasty smell belongs to someone called Kelvin.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kelvin was the physicist who gave his name to the temperature scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Lord Kelvin, the Victorian physicist, is one instance of a researcher in science.

clue.text: The last word in steam engines

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words steam engines

explanation.surface: The ultimate in steam engines.
explanation.definitionFit: The word said at the end of a prayer is literally the final word.

clue.text: The man's too rich — repeatedly making reductions is important

parts.note: his is the possessive of 'he', the man

indicators.note: each of the two words loses a letter, one cut after another

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man who is too wealthy keeps cutting costs, which matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly making reductions' cuts one O from TOO and the H from RICH, leaving TO and RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a historic event is a momentous or significant one.

clue.text: Working on DPhils — they're supposedly intelligent

indicators.note: these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Doctoral students at work are said to be clever.
explanation.walkthrough: A DPhil is the Oxford doctorate; the clever ones here are sea mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: These marine mammals are widely reputed to be among the cleverest animals.

clue.text: Foul allowed? Not at first

indicators.note: tells us to drop the opening letter of the word for allowed

parts.note: something allowed by the rules is lawful

explanation.surface: A sports fan queries whether a foul was permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something very bad or unpleasant, as in foul or dreadful weather.

clue.text: Common virus Neal developed

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters have evolved into a new form

explanation.surface: A man called Neal has caught a widespread virus.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something common to all is universal, shared by everyone.

clue.text: Sorting out musical instrument — then I perform songs

parts.note: an organ is a keyboard musical instrument
to sing is to perform songs

explanation.surface: Someone tidying up a church instrument says they will then give a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sorting things out means arranging them into order.

clue.text: Do be quiet to get lolly

parts.note: taken as written
sh is the instruction to be quiet

explanation.surface: Keep quiet and you'll be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lolly' is British slang for money, not a sweet on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British slang words for money or cash.

clue.text: Kind deed by sort of seaman? Promising

parts.note: a favour is a kind deed
an able seaman is a naval rank

explanation.surface: A sailor does someone a good turn, which bodes well.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: favourable signs are encouraging and promising.

clue.text: Exercise and sport in air, running around causing this?

definitions.text: Exercise and sport in air, running around causing this?

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: running about suggests the letters are moving out of order

explanation.surface: Playing games outdoors and dashing about makes you sweat.
explanation.definitionFit: Exertion such as running around brings on sweating, the bodily result the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Extra footballer stretches and takes off

parts.note: a substitute or sub is an extra player
tracts are stretches of land

explanation.surface: A reserve player warms up and then undresses.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to take a number off another is to deduct it.

clue.text: Cause incident

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to bring something about

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning bring about and a noun for a particular event.

clue.text: In dreadful court, getting evasive

parts.note: taken as written
dire means dreadful

explanation.surface: A witness in a terrible court proves slippery.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an evasive answer avoids the point instead of being direct.

clue.text: In regret, almost buy gift

indicators.note: one piece goes into the middle of the word for regret

parts.note: contrition is remorse or regret

indicators.note: the last letter of the word buy is lost

explanation.surface: Someone sorry for something buys a present by way of apology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gift' is the definition: a contribution is something given; 'In' and 'almost' both act on the clipped purchase word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a contribution is something given, such as a donation or present.

clue.text: Idle MD's developing waist

indicators.note: the letters are developing into a new form

parts.note: MD, a medical doctor, contributes its two letters

explanation.surface: A lazy doctor is getting a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the middle of the body is the waist area.

clue.text: Snake cult ignoring leader's view

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake

indicators.note: says to drop the first letter of the word for cult

parts.note: a sect is a religious cult

explanation.surface: A snake-worshipping group disregards its head's opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an aspect is a view or outlook, as of a house facing south.

clue.text: A no-good royal? Similar

indicators.note: says to remove the letter for good from the word for royal

parts.note: a king is a royal

explanation.surface: A useless monarch is asked whether he resembles another.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: two things that are related in nature or character are similar.

clue.text: Estate agents display these traits

definitions.meaning: houses and flats are on show in an estate agent's window

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both real-estate holdings for sale and the characteristic qualities of a thing.

clue.text: Greek letter was first to be collected

parts.note: pi is a Greek letter
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: A Greek letter was the first to be gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things piled up have been heaped together or gathered.

clue.text: Pen beginning to expand — you might notice it on the lid

definitions.text: you might notice it on the lid

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: takes the first letter of expand

explanation.surface: A pigpen starting to grow, something seen on the lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A small inflamed swelling at the edge of the eyelid.

clue.text: I hollow and I hollo — almost the same

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for hollo is dropped

parts.note: to hollo is to call out

explanation.surface: Someone hollowing and shouting finds it all much of a muchness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollo' is an old variant of hallo, a shout; CALL loses its last L.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things exactly alike are said to be the same.

clue.text: Mark woodland animal with no tail

indicators.note: means the last letter of the animal's name is cut off

parts.note: a badger is a burrowing woodland mammal

explanation.surface: Someone tags a forest creature that has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a distinguishing mark or emblem worn to show membership or rank.

clue.text: Fruitcakes from northern States

parts.note: to state something is to utter it

explanation.surface: Christmas cakes imported from the American north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcakes' is slang for eccentric people, and 'States' is a verb, not America.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal slang for people regarded as mad or eccentric.

clue.text: Most intense river disease

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, Wales and England
pest is an old word for plague or pestilence

explanation.surface: The worst illness comes from a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the deepest feelings are the strongest or most intense.
